line_move_forecast.rationale: The line has done its moving early: San Francisco opened -5.5 (DraftKings via ESPN pickcenter open line, confirmed in the live ESPN summary fetch on Oct 16) and was bet up to -7.5 before T0, and the spread has not moved since - identical SF -7.5 at all eight of yesterday's archived observations (line-archive snapshot captures 15:19, 16:20 and 19:15 CT and flat captures 17:15, 18:13, 19:17, 22:15 and 23:14 UTC, all DraftKings via ESPN) and still SF -7.5 in today's live ESPN fetch, with the total at 51.5 (opened 50.5). The moneyline has kept drifting the same way, from SF -250 / WAS +205 at open to SF -440 / WAS +340 in today's fetch, after sitting at -425 / +330 through yesterday's archive. R0 is INSUFFICIENT_DATA (zero completed trajectories), so there is no measured base rate to defer to and this forecast stays near the middle by design. FLAT carries the largest mass (0.40): the spread itself has been pinned for a full day at 7.5, and the remaining news flow (practice reports, the final injury report, Monday inactives) is at least as likely to be absorbed via the total or the price as via the spread. But 72 hours remain on a standalone Monday-night game, so a move of 0.5 or more in some direction is collectively more likely (0.60) than an unchanged close. The directional lean is slightly toward HOME (0.32 vs 0.28): the only drift observed this week ran one way, toward San Francisco (spread -5.5 to -7.5, through the key number 7; moneyline -250 to -440), and continuation of an established one-way drift is judged a more common late-week pattern than a full reversal back through 7 toward Washington. That lean is stated as judgment, not measurement. This v2 revision changes no probability: it replaces v1's secondary-source opening-line citation and Oct 15 moneyline with the primary-source ESPN pickcenter open/close values from the Oct 16 live fetch, whose content reached the stamping worker after v1 was stamped.
